subject: anti-zionism
notes: Anti-Zionism, as it functions in practice, operates primarily as a causal attribution engine rather than a coherent geopolitical position — it substitutes moral clarity for strategic thinking, serves as a flexible container for unrelated ideological grievances, and produces systematically worse geopolitical reasoning in countries and movements that adopt it as an organizing principle.

subject: anti-zionism
notes: Anti-Zionism provides a morally simplified framework (oppressor/oppressed binary) that displaces cost-benefit strategic analysis, leading adopters to prioritize symbolic moral positioning over pragmatic geopolitical calculation.

subject: anti-zionism
notes: Anti-Zionism functions as an ideological attractor that absorbs and unifies disparate grievances — anti-imperialism, anti-capitalism, decolonialism, anti-Americanism — providing a single causal node onto which structurally unrelated complaints can be projected.

subject: anti-zionist-adopters
notes: Countries and movements that adopt anti-Zionism as an organizing principle demonstrably produce worse geopolitical reasoning — misallocating diplomatic capital, misjudging alliances, and failing to advance their own stated interests — compared to actors that treat Israel/Palestine as one issue among many.

subject: anti-zionism
notes: Anti-Zionism does not produce consistent policy prescriptions across its adherents: it ranges from one-state advocacy to eliminationism to mere diplomatic opposition, suggesting it functions not as a geopolitical position but as an identity marker or coalition signal.

subject: causal-attribution-engines
notes: Monocausal explanatory frameworks — where a single actor or force is treated as the root cause of many disparate problems — systematically degrade analytical reasoning by reducing complex multi-variable situations to a single causal chain, a well-documented pattern in cognitive science and political psychology.
